solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Newspaper feature on screen is hit in a big way

indicators.note: in a down or across charade 'on' sets one piece after another; here the feature follows the screen

parts.note: a wall is a barrier that screens one area from another
an op-ed is the opinion page or piece opposite a newspaper's editorials

explanation.surface: A newspaper article showing on a screen proves a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper feature' is an op-ed, an opinion column; 'on' puts it after the screen in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be walloped is to be struck very hard, a heavy blow being a hit in a big way.

clue.text: Fermenting malt a success, repaying the effort

parts.note: wort is the malt infusion that ferments into beer
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: Brewing beer from malt turns out a success that justified the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth it justifies the time and trouble, so it repays the effort.

clue.text: Dropping by in hall, one treated smashingly?

indicators.note: dropping the word by asks for those letters to be left out of the hall word

parts.note: a lobby is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: Someone dropping by the hall is given a smashing welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashingly' looks like praise, but in tennis a lob is the high shot an opponent may smash.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a high lob that falls short invites the opponent's overhead smash.

clue.text: Supreme order to speed with energy through parts of bible?

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
to nip is to go quickly

indicators.note: the energy letter runs through the middle, between the two testaments

parts.note: OT and NT are the Old and New Testaments
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A divine command to hurry, run through sections of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme' reads as an adjective on 'order' but is the definition; 'order' is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means all-powerful, the supreme authority above all others.

clue.text: Support skinning mustelids

indicators.note: skinning strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: weasels belong to the mustelid family, with stoats and otters

explanation.surface: Something that helps in stripping the pelts from weasels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinning' removes the outer W and S of WEASELS.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a painting or board, a kind of support.

clue.text: Influential group causes custom to be observed only on the left

indicators.note: seeing only the left side of each word means keeping just the front half of each one

explanation.surface: A powerful faction makes people follow a custom only on one side of the political spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed only on the left' keeps the left halves: CAU from CAUSES and CUS from CUSTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a group of party members meeting to decide policy, often wielding outsized influence.

clue.text: Quiet call to notice a piece of skirt

parts.note: the hem is the turned-up edge of a skirt

explanation.surface: A soft wolf-whistle aimed at a woman, 'a piece of skirt' in old slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of skirt' is dated slang for a woman, but here it is just the hem.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the small cough people make to attract attention discreetly.

clue.text: Possibility of night called for this in power cut?

indicators.note: a possibility of the words is one of their possible arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: When the power fails at night, people resort to this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibility of' signals a rearrangement of NIGHT CALLED; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When the electricity fails, candles are lit to see by.

clue.text: Organise outdoor entertainment, having good forecast

parts.note: to set something up is to organise it
a fair, with rides and stalls, is an outdoor entertainment

explanation.surface: Arranging a fete when the weather forecast is promising.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes settled weather, as in a barometer reading predicting sunshine.

clue.text: What's up, old battered fighter?

indicators.note: a battered thing is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A greeting to a beaten-up veteran boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges WHATSUP and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, a type of fighter.

clue.text: How to greet Eskimo? One that's heartless may keep stressing an error?

parts.note: the traditional Inuit greeting is said to be rubbing noses, so how to greet one is to rub one's nose

indicators.note: a word without its heart loses its middle letter, here from the people's name

parts.note: the Inuit are the Arctic people formerly called Eskimos

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Arctic greetings that turns into a remark about someone who harps on a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle U out of INUIT, leaving INIT. 'One that's ... may' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub someone's nose in it is the idiom for repeatedly reminding them of a blunder.

clue.text: Undercooked dish taken round a part of mouth

parts.note: food not cooked enough, such as vegetables, stays hard

indicators.note: the dish's letters go round the a, surrounding it

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: An underdone dish is sent back round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' puts A inside PLATE to give PALATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard palate is the bony front section of the roof of the mouth.

clue.text: Girl full of love after perusing location of ballad

parts.note: perusing means reading

indicators.note: the girl word is filled with the love letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A young woman is smitten after reading something.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde wrote 'The Ballad of Reading Gaol'; Reading is an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's poem was written about the prison where he was held, the place the ballad concerns.

clue.text: It could be guilty enjoyment — not certain

indicators.note: 'not certain' asks for the word meaning certain to be left out of the enjoyment word

parts.note: pleasure means enjoyment
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A guilty pleasure is an enjoyment one is unsure about owning up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be guilty' points at a court plea, while the surface reads 'guilty enjoyment' as a guilty pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: In court a defendant enters a plea, guilty being one of the possible pleas.

clue.text: Old and decrepit, fail to answer film star with animation

indicators.note: something decrepit has fallen apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: to duck a question is to avoid answering it

explanation.surface: An aged movie actor, too frail to reply, though still lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrepit' rearranges OLD AND into DONALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Duck is the Disney cartoon character, an animated screen star.

clue.text: "To Daisy!" he may cry

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower of the daisy family

explanation.surface: Someone raises a glass to a woman called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' reads as a woman's name but is the flower ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is a person proposing a toast, who cries out 'To ...!' when raising a glass.

clue.text: Approval from the palace to secure a safe place for Charles

indicators.note: the approval holds the a firmly inside it

parts.note: a royal OK is approval from the monarch

explanation.surface: Royal assent is needed to buy a secure residence for the prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II hid in an oak tree at Boscobel after losing the Battle of Worcester in 1651.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Oak is the tree that hid the future Charles II from his pursuers.

clue.text: Hands separately interrupting might make someone suspicious

indicators.note: separately says the two hand letters do not stay together but go in at different points
the hand letters break into the word for might, sitting inside it

parts.note: power means might
R and L are the right and left hands

explanation.surface: Waving one's hands about while butting in can make a person seem shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' gives R and L (right, left); 'interrupting' puts them in POWER and 'separately' splits them, R after the P and L after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A prowler is someone lurking about with apparent criminal intent, a suspicious character.

clue.text: See round most of private little wood

indicators.note: the seeing word goes round the shortened private word

parts.note: to spy is to see

indicators.note: most of the word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: inner means private, as in one's inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a small private woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' here means inner, as in private thoughts, not a soldier; 'most of' drops its last letter and 'round' wraps the seeing word about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small copse or thicket of trees.

clue.text: Old teacher's concession welcome, by the way

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Old teacher is'

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a concession
hi is a word of welcome
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A retired teacher mentions a concession being welcome, as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' reads as an aside, but 'by' just places ST beside HI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sophists were paid teachers of rhetoric and philosophy in ancient Greece.

clue.text: In war, not a point of view to dispute

indicators.note: 'not a' tells us to drop the letter a from war

parts.note: an angle is a point of view or slant

explanation.surface: In wartime, there is no single viewpoint left to argue over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' leaves WR from WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to argue or dispute noisily and at length.

clue.text: Church officer and laity, not content but getting on

parts.note: an elder is an official in a Presbyterian church

indicators.note: without its contents, only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A church official and the lay members are unhappy but carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means the inside; 'getting on' means ageing, not coping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on is advancing in years, which is what elderly describes.

clue.text: Initially exposing omission, turning over part of text

indicators.note: the combined letters are read in the opposite direction
the start of exposing supplies its first letter

parts.note: a gap is an omission

explanation.surface: Exposing a gap in the text when you turn over to the next sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses EGAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is one side of a leaf in a book, a portion of the text.

clue.text: Made clear one clue is convoluted, not new

indicators.note: something convoluted is twisted, so these letters are tangled up

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
dated means old-fashioned, not new

explanation.surface: A setter explains that a twisted clue is past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convoluted' rearranges CLUE into ELUC; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to explain or throw light on something.

clue.text: Furry creature, evasive and revolting, from the south

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from the bottom upwards turns the word over

parts.note: people who revolt are up in arms, so to be revolting is to be up

explanation.surface: A shy fluffy animal stages an uprising in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' means rising up, not disgusting; 'from the south' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent with dense fur, farmed for it.

clue.text: Draw arm or leg, as told

indicators.note: as told means as spoken, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: an arm or a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: An art instruction to sketch a limb as directed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a sketch class but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To limn is a literary word for to depict or paint.

clue.text: Mathematical feature in a made up edition

parts.note: imaginary means made up
a number is an issue or edition of a magazine

explanation.surface: A mathematical feature appears in a fabricated issue.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginary number is a multiple of the square root of minus one, a concept in mathematics.

clue.text: Receive deliveries of book and wait for periodical appearance

indicators.note: letters appearing periodically means every other letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Taking in a book delivery and awaiting the next issue of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodical' suggests a magazine but signals alternate letters of WAIT, giving AT.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the batsman faces, or receives, the bowler's deliveries, which is to bat.

clue.text: Nearly everything in pavilion is bent

indicators.note: the shortened everything sits inside the tent

parts.note: a pavilion can be a large tent, as at a fete

indicators.note: nearly the whole word drops its last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Almost everything inside the cricket pavilion has been bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is bent' reads as broken, but 'bent' is a noun: a natural aptitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural aptitude or flair, as is a talent.

clue.text: Shooting a thousand wild turkeys

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter goes after a thousand wild turkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TURKEYS into USKETRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry is the art or practice of firing muskets, i.e. shooting.
